title: Microsoft Foundry Model Deployment Decision
summary: Select and govern a Microsoft Foundry model deployment using current catalog availability, workload evaluation, identity, region, capacity, cost, and recovery evidence.
prerequisites: An Azure subscription and approved tenant boundary
A defined workload, region, data class, and budget
Permission to inspect catalog availability and quota

sections.title: Start from the actual tenant, region, and resource type
paragraphs: Microsoft Foundry catalog visibility and deployment options depend on resource type, model publisher, region, offer, subscription access, quota, and lifecycle. Confirm the option in the target tenant rather than assuming that a model visible in documentation is deployable everywhere. Standard, provisioned-throughput, managed-compute, and preview paths have different controls. For this production exercise, only the explicitly allowed GA lifecycle passes. Preview, retired, missing, and unknown lifecycle values are rejected.

Treat catalog visibility as discovery evidence, not deployment authority. A catalog record cannot prove remaining tenant quota, marketplace-terms acceptance, application-identity access, network access, data-boundary compatibility, or workload fitness. Record those as separate Boolean gates. Missing, unknown, or non-Boolean gate evidence fails closed before price or ranking is considered. No tenant, subscription, catalog, quota, identity, network, marketplace, deployment, or API was probed for this lesson.

Record the exact publisher, model, version, SKU, lifecycle, deployment shape, route scope, and reviewed data-boundary attribute. Microsoft Phi, Meta, DeepSeek, Mistral, Qwen, NVIDIA, and Z.ai are broad research starting points only. Their availability is catalog-dependent, and this guide makes no universal availability claim. Candidate attributes must be reviewed against an independently documented case policy rather than accepted as self-asserted compliance.

The bounded PowerShell example uses the Microsoft-documented read-only list-models command, requests JSON explicitly, and iterates every returned SKU. It requires Azure CLI 2.60 or later and appropriate deployment-management read access. It does not retrieve keys, create, update, delete, or deploy anything, and it does not call inference. Listing name, format, version, and SKU still does not establish quota, terms acceptance, application access, or workload fitness.
This is a bounded read-only discovery example, not evidence of actual execution. It intentionally contains no key-listing, output of secrets, create, update, delete, deployment, or inference action.

code.label: Read-only model and SKU discovery

sections.callout: Catalog visibility is only the first gate. Actual deployability requires dated tenant, region, resource, data-boundary, quota, identity, network, marketplace, lifecycle, and workload evidence.

sections.title: Evaluate the workload and capacity shape
paragraphs: Use catalog benchmarks only to discover candidates. Set an independent trusted workload threshold before ranking, then test representative application inputs, safety behavior, tool trajectories, latency, throughput, failures, quota behavior, cost units, and recovery. A highest-ranked option is not sufficient: it must meet the threshold and every hard gate. The offline evaluator returns only CONDITIONAL_RECOMMENDATION or REFUSE_ALL. Neither result authorizes a real deployment.

All following records are fictional snapshots with opaque fictional model, version, and SKU identifiers. Case A permits global or regional routing and either reviewed global or regional data handling. Its threshold is 0.85. Candidate bursty-global-standard has publisher Microsoft, model Fictional-Phi-Candidate, version snapshot-A1, SKU Opaque-GlobalStandard-A, standard shape, GA lifecycle, score 0.92, and all hard gates true. It is conditionally recommended. Bursty-global-preview loses exactly because preview is outside the allowed production lifecycle, despite score 0.99. Bursty-global-provisioned loses exactly because its score 0.90 is below the winner's 0.92. Its fictional reservation is 2.00 USD per reservation hour for 720 reservation hours: 2.00 x 720 = 1,440.00 USD, paid in full regardless of the stated 50 percent utilization. Standard cost is UNKNOWN, so the exercise does not treat it as zero or claim that standard is cheaper.

Case B requires a regional route and a reviewed regional data boundary. Its threshold is 0.85. Regulated-regional has publisher Mistral, model Fictional-Mistral-Candidate, version snapshot-B1, SKU Opaque-RegionalStandard-B, standard shape, GA lifecycle, score 0.88, and passing gates, so it is conditionally recommended. Regulated-global-standard scores 0.95 but loses exactly because its reviewed global route scope and global data boundary are not allowed by the regional policy. Regulated-preview loses exactly because preview is outside the production lifecycle. Thus independent policy compatibility overrides rank.

The changed-input task is independent: suppose the data owner documents a new workload classification that permits both global and regional routing and both reviewed global and regional data boundaries. Change those two policy lists, not a candidate's self-asserted region flag. Recompute the decision. The key is changed-regulated: CONDITIONAL_RECOMMENDATION regulated-global-standard, because that candidate now satisfies the documented policy and its score 0.95 exceeds 0.88. The preview candidate remains rejected.

If a required gate such as quota_ok is None, the fixture is invalid evidence and the result is REFUSE_ALL with a control error. Valid but low-quality or lifecycle-ineligible sets also produce REFUSE_ALL. Never convert a provisioned capacity unit to TPM or another throughput unit without dated authoritative conversion evidence. The exercise compares only its explicit fictional reservation-hour arithmetic and keeps utilization separate from the amount owed.

sections.callout: The score, costs, identities, candidate attributes, and catalog snapshots are fictional. A conditional recommendation remains subject to independent tenant, security, data, marketplace, quota, application, operational, and deployment verification.

sections.title: Expected offline output
paragraphs: Compare your run with this expected output.

code.label: Expected offline output
code.code:
Exact expected output, without claiming execution:
bursty: CONDITIONAL_RECOMMENDATION bursty-global-standard
  bursty-global-preview: REJECT lifecycle preview is not allowed by production policy
  bursty-global-provisioned: NOT_SELECTED fit_score 0.90 is below winner 0.92
regulated: CONDITIONAL_RECOMMENDATION regulated-regional
  regulated-global-standard: REJECT route_scope global is not allowed by case policy; data_boundary global is not allowed by case policy
  regulated-preview: REJECT lifecycle preview is not allowed by production policy
unknown-evidence: REFUSE_ALL (CONTROL_ERROR: unknown or non-Boolean hard gate: quota_ok)
changed-regulated: CONDITIONAL_RECOMMENDATION regulated-global-standard
  regulated-preview: REJECT lifecycle preview is not allowed by production policy
  regulated-regional: NOT_SELECTED fit_score 0.88 is below winner 0.95
negative tests: PASS
Uncaught assertion failures make Python exit nonzero.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes target tenant and region, resource type, exact catalog item and lifecycle, offer terms, deployment shape, quota, identity and network controls, representative evaluation, load and cost results, stable application route, owner, and expiry.

Verify authentication and authorization from the application identity, network restrictions, request and content behavior, observability, quota failure, failover, and final user result. On failure, stop promotion, restore the verified route, reconcile possible tool writes, and delete or scale down only the failed deployment after evidence is preserved.

Complete the preserved decision template with dated evidence. Use UNKNOWN rather than inventing a value. The evaluator accepts only standard, provisioned, and managed_compute shapes even though the preserved blank template includes OTHER for recording and escalation. Keep the stable deployment name separate from exact publisher, model, version, SKU, lifecycle, and offer.

For Case A, the exact losing reasons are an unapproved preview lifecycle and a lower trusted workload score for the provisioned alternative. For Case B, the exact losing reasons are incompatible global route and data-boundary attributes, plus an unapproved preview lifecycle. If quota, identity, network, marketplace terms, regional compatibility, data-boundary evidence, or representative workload evidence is unknown, refuse all until evidence is supplied.

Provider-neutral transfer uses the same order: define workload policy and data boundary, discover account-specific candidates, preserve exact identifiers, validate containers and hard gates, derive policy compatibility from reviewed attributes, apply a trusted threshold, compare costs only in supported units, verify the application route, and retain recovery evidence. Microsoft Foundry names and Azure CLI syntax are specific to this example.

The cited Microsoft documentation supports the deployment concepts, discovery command, and benchmark context. It does not establish the fictional candidates as real offers, their availability in any tenant or region, remaining quota, accepted terms, application access, workload fitness, or current prices. Those facts are UNKNOWN until established by dated tenant-specific records and independent verification.

This is the original blank template, preserved verbatim. Fill every field from evidence, retain explicit UNKNOWN values, and escalate unsupported OTHER shapes rather than passing them to the offline evaluator.

code.label: Foundry deployment decision record
code.code:
Task: [WORKLOAD AND DEPLOYMENT DECISION]
Scope: [AZURE TENANT, SUBSCRIPTION, REGION, RESOURCE TYPE, AND DATA CLASS]
Permissions: [DEPLOYER IDENTITY, RBAC, NETWORK, MARKETPLACE, AND SPEND AUTHORITY]
Candidate: [PUBLISHER, EXACT MODEL/VERSION, LIFECYCLE, AND OFFER]
Deployment shape: [STANDARD | PROVISIONED | MANAGED COMPUTE | OTHER]
Capacity: [QUOTA, THROUGHPUT, CONCURRENCY, LATENCY, AND BURST]
Evaluation: [APPLICATION CASES, CATALOG EVIDENCE, THRESHOLDS, AND COST]
Stop conditions: [UNAPPROVED PREVIEW, QUOTA GAP, DATA/REGION GAP, OR FAILED GATE]
Verification: [IDENTITY/NETWORK TEST, LOAD TEST, EVALUATION, AND USER POSTCONDITION]
Recovery: [ROUTE TO VERIFIED DEPLOYMENT, RECONCILE STATE, AND REMOVE FAILED CAPACITY]

sections.callout: Offline results are not deployment approvals. Responsible tenant, security, data, marketplace, finance, application, and operations owners must independently verify and authorize any real deployment.
